clue.text: Clearly an obstacle for a working girl prepared to go all the way?

definitions.text: Clearly an obstacle for a working girl prepared to go all the way?

parts.words: Clearly an obstacle for a working girl prepared to go all the way?
parts.note: an invisible (hence 'clearly', as through clear material) barrier stopping an ambitious career woman from rising right to the top, dressed up as something racier

explanation.surface: A coy, saucy hint about what stands in the way of a girl willing to go all the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working girl' and 'go all the way' hint at sex, but the girl is simply a woman with a job who wants to reach the top; 'clearly' points to a barrier you can see through.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an unseen barrier that keeps women from senior posts, so it is a transparent obstacle to a career woman's rise.

clue.text: Baboons' blue, top grade pin up

definitions.note: the definition is the possessive 'Baboons'', and with the 's read as 'is' it stands for the plural name of the animals

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' says the whole string of pieces is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: blue means sad, low in spirits
A is the top grade in an exam
pin is slang for a leg

explanation.surface: A sad-looking baboon, an excellent specimen, appears in a pin-up picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the run SAD + A + LEG, giving GELADAS; the apostrophe in 'Baboons'' is a link meaning 'are', so the definition is just the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Geladas are Ethiopian grass-eating monkeys commonly called gelada baboons, so they are a kind of baboon.

clue.text: Hit tax haven with no capital: left empty

indicators.note: having no capital letter means the opening letter of the word is lost

parts.note: Nassau, capital of the Bahamas, is a well-known offshore tax haven

indicators.note: a word made empty keeps only its outermost letters, its first and last

explanation.surface: Someone attacks an offshore tax haven, leaving it bankrupt and deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' tempts you to think of a city (Nassau is one), but here it means the first letter, removed by 'with no capital' to leave ASSAU; 'empty' strips 'left' to LT.
explanation.definitionFit: To assault someone is to hit or attack them, so the noun or verb fits the swap.

clue.text: Racket's ideal location? Maybe hundreds and thousands given to grass

parts.note: hundreds and thousands are tiny sugar sprinkles for cakes, an example of sweets
grass is slang for cannabis, also called pot

explanation.surface: A recipe-like note about sprinkles and grass, framed by a question about where a racket belongs.
explanation.walkthrough: Hundreds and thousands are what Americans call sprinkles, so 'Maybe' marks them as an example of sweets. 'Racket' suggests noise or crime but is the tennis racket.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet spot is the part of a racket's strings that hits the ball best, its ideal point of contact.

clue.text: End of three months and Wood not quite burnt out

definitions.meaning: September, November and December all finish with the same five letters, so those letters are the end shared by three months
a smouldering scrap of wood left glowing in a dying fire

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a playful one: the common ending of the three autumn and winter months spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing remnant of a fire is wood that has not finished burning; and the letters close three month names.

clue.text: Admitted switching title on

indicators.note: switching places means the letters of 'title on' change positions

explanation.surface: An admission about swapping a title around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching' rearranges TITLE ON to LET INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone into a place is to admit them, so the past forms match as verbs.

clue.text: As head teachers collectively enjoy

parts.note: the NUT, the National Union of Teachers, is a British teachers' trade union
to like something is to enjoy it

explanation.surface: Teachers band together to enjoy acting as head of school.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT was the main teachers' union in England and Wales. 'Head' looks like a headteacher, but it is the head as in skull, slang 'nut'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut is slang for the head, so something resembling a nut is in the manner of a head.

clue.text: I don't know what it is to be slim, with the ability to stick to dance

definitions.text: I don't know what it is

parts.note: slim means thin
gummy describes something sticky, able to stick
a jig is a lively folk dance

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by a gadget is told it helps you get slim and stick to dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a placeholder name for an item whose proper name the speaker cannot recall, like 'whatsit'.

clue.text: Religious area, yes, out in space

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the gap

parts.note: a hole is a space or gap

indicators.note: out means messed up, so the three letters of 'yes' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone affirms that a holy place exists out in space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'space' looks like outer space, but it is just a gap; 'out' signals the jumble of 'yes' and 'in' sets it inside the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy See is the jurisdiction of the Pope in Rome, a religious domain.

clue.text: An English city, however topsy-turvy, offers grime-removing facility

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England

indicators.note: topsy-turvy means upside down, so the word for 'however' is turned back to front

parts.note: however means but

explanation.surface: An English city, despite being in disarray, provides a place to get clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topsy-turvy' turns the word for 'however' round. Bath, a Somerset city, is famous for its Roman baths, a fitting touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathtub is where you wash dirt off your body, so it is a facility for removing grime.

clue.text: "Obi", the cryptic clue setter's way to show nature's rich mixture?

parts.note: the clue words show OBI, which is what you get from a 'diversity', a varying, of BIO, the way a setter would write an anagram

explanation.surface: A remark on how a setter might clue a Japanese sash, which turns into a word for nature's variety.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: BIO plus DIVERSITY (as an anagram indicator) gives OBI, which the clue prints.
explanation.definitionFit: The variety of living species in a habitat is a rich natural mix, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Bound to, as it might otherwise be put

definitions.text: Bound to, as it might otherwise be put

indicators.text: as it might otherwise be put
indicators.note: put otherwise means placed another way, so the letters of 'Bound to' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone offers another way of saying 'bound to'.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of BOUND TO gives the phrase, and the whole clue also defines it as another way of saying 'bound to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is bound to happen is saying it will certainly happen, another way of putting it.

clue.text: Or no movement is without sound of this short musical piece

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so one piece sits around the other
movement means the letters move about, rearranging 'Or no'

parts.note: a din is a loud sound

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether a short piece of music lacks a movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks musical but rearranges OR NO to RONO, and 'without' (outside) puts it round DIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondino is a short rondo, a brief musical composition.

clue.text: Tip: hike with a crowd

parts.note: to hike prices is to put them up
a set is a group of people, a crowd

explanation.surface: Advice on going for a walk with a group of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like advice, but it is the verb to overturn.
explanation.definitionFit: To tip a cup is to knock it over, which is to overturn it.

clue.text: Composer's "Zing!" covered by ailing Presley (not the last one)

definitions.note: the definition includes 's as 'is', so it stands for the composer

indicators.note: covered by means the energetic word sits inside the jumble
ailing means unwell, out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
not the last means the final letter of Presley is dropped

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
zing and go both mean energy, vim

explanation.surface: A composer's zest is smothered by a sickly Elvis Presley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the last' drops the singer's final letter; 'one' adds I, and 'ailing' scrambles the result to PERLESI, which 'covered by' wraps round the word for zing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pergolesi was an eighteenth-century Italian composer of the Stabat Mater, so he is an example of a composer.

clue.text: IRA turn out with Paisley — new departure, a novel state!

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the gathered letters are rearranged

parts.note: IRA, the Irish Republican Army, taken as written

indicators.note: a departure means the letter leaves the name

parts.note: Ian Paisley was a Northern Ireland unionist leader, so Paisley gives his first name

explanation.surface: Northern Ireland politics: the IRA turning out alongside Paisley would be a new departure, a novel state of affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'departure' drops N (new) from IAN, leaving IA; 'out' rearranges IRA + TURN + IA. Ruritania is the made-up kingdom of Anthony Hope's novel The Prisoner of Zenda.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the imaginary country in Anthony Hope's novel, a state existing only in fiction.

clue.text: In the distance, US-style officer with a big drip coming down the mountain

definitions.text: big drip coming down the mountain

indicators.note: In puts the officer and companions inside the measure of distance

parts.note: the metre, a unit of distance, is spelt meter in American English
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: In the distance, an American officer is seen with a tall, dull companion coming down the mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big drip' suggests a bore, but it is water running off a glacier; 'In' puts the officer, W and A inside the American spelling of the distance unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Meltwater is water from melting snow or glaciers, which runs down from the peaks.

clue.text: Country — a vast, bleak, cold region — needs new leader

indicators.note: a new leader means the first letter of the region is replaced by another

parts.note: Siberia is the vast, bleak, cold region of northern Russia

explanation.surface: A topical comment that a vast, bleak country needs a fresh leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs new leader' swaps the first letter of SIBERIA; the new letter is not clued. The surface fits 2006, when Liberia had just got a new leader, Ellen Johnson Sirleaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a country on the west coast of Africa, so it is an example of a nation.

clue.text: Organised fatwa over, for example, uplifting poetic transportation

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second
organised means put into a new order, so the letters of fatwa are rearranged
in a down clue, uplifting means the piece is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: An organised religious edict, among other things, makes for uplifting poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' rearranges FATWA to WAFTA; 'uplifting' turns EG to GE, placed beneath it ('over').
explanation.definitionFit: Waftage is a poetic word for the act of being carried gently through air or over water, a kind of conveyance.

clue.text: Well-informed about scratchy ape developing insects

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for well-informed is reversed

parts.note: to be up on a subject is to be well-informed about it

indicators.note: scratchy means rough, irritable, so the letters of ape are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone knowledgeable about an itchy ape watches insects develop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses UP to PU; 'scratchy' rearranges APE to PAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupae are insects at the stage between larva and adult, so they are still developing.

clue.text: Politician's first to get shelved — swore not to drink?

indicators.note: first means take just the opening letter of the word

parts.note: something put on a ledge, a shelf, is ledged

explanation.surface: A politician's first plan gets shelved: he vowed not to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'take the pledge' is to promise to give up alcohol, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the pledge means vowing to abstain from alcohol, so one who pledged gave such a promise.

clue.text: Space probe taking look round satellite at noon

indicators.note: round means the word for look goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to peer is to look closely
Io is a moon of Jupiter, a satellite

explanation.surface: A space probe takes a look around a satellite at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: Io is one of Jupiter's large moons; 'round' wraps the look around the moon and noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Pioneer was a series of NASA space probes, including those that first flew past Jupiter and Saturn.

clue.text: Favoured employment of minors that results in 1 across?

definitions.text: Favoured employment of minors that results in 1 across?

parts.words: Favoured employment of minors that results in 1 across?
parts.note: posts handed out to friends and cronies, read as work given to young males rather than girls, which would keep women from rising to the top

explanation.surface: Child labour that produces something made of glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minors' hints at children, but the phrase means jobs given to pals; 1 across is the barrier facing working women, which such favouritism creates.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means positions given to friends or associates rather than on merit, favoured employment.

clue.text: Contractual modification to remove King Edward

parts.note: to rid is to remove or free from
ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A contract change that gets rid of a king.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the royal cipher for any King Edward (or Queen Elizabeth); King Edward is also a potato variety, a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is a clause added to a contract or bill, modifying its terms.

clue.text: See 21
Former musical star returning paper light

indicators.note: returning means the word for paper goes back to front

parts.note: a rag is a newspaper, especially a poor one
to light on something is to land on it

explanation.surface: A one-time musical star brings back a newspaper and a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses RAG to GAR. 'light' looks like a lamp, but it is the verb to settle. Judy Garland starred in The Wizard of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: Judy Garland was a celebrated Hollywood singer and film actress of the past.

clue.text: Pass up information about desks losing their right side

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for information is reversed

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: losing the right-hand half leaves only the first half of the word

parts.note: lecterns are reading desks

explanation.surface: Information about classroom desks missing one side gets passed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses GEN to NEG; 'losing their right side' halves LECTERNS to LECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect an opportunity is to pass it up, to disregard it.

clue.text: Tear line on calculator: it won't extend beyond 1 across for some

definitions.text: it won't extend beyond 1 across for some

parts.note: to tear is to rush, to career along
an adder is a machine that adds, a calculator

explanation.surface: A rip in the line on a calculator display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' looks like a rip but means to rush. 1 across is the invisible barrier that stops many women climbing higher.
explanation.definitionFit: The career ladder is the series of promotions in a job, and for some women it stops at an invisible barrier.
